critical-bundle-gzip.reason:
SPEC §21.1: 516 KB gzip against the 350 KB budget, 355 KB of it mb_bg.wasm. The WASM doubled between M0 and M7 and mb-crdt's yrs is the suspect; the JS has grown with the M7 shell. Untried levers: opt-level s/z for the wasm build, wasm-opt -Oz, and splitting mb-crdt out of the initial chunk. Compression has landed and did not move this number: it is a gzip budget, and what changed is that the server now sends gzip. The wire went from 1.39 MB to 524.8 KB (SPEC 21.1, 21.7); the budget is still 350 KB and this is still 47% over it. Carried, not ignored: this harness exists so §21.3's measure-before-and-after can be satisfied before anyone touches opt-level. Tolerance is 0% for bytes, so any growth from here fails the build.

Raised by 1,399 bytes (526,850 → 528,249) for the inline task view: the node view in web/src/editor/task-view.ts, its chip helpers, and the CSS for both. That is §10.2 — a checkbox and metadata chips — which the application shipped without through M7, so this is a required feature and not an optional one, and 1.4 KB is proportionate to it. It is measured rather than estimated, and it changes none of the reasoning above: the 355 KB of WASM is still where the budget is lost and still where the fix is. Re-measured after compression landed: unchanged, as expected, because this line is the static gzip figure and always was. The next thing that can move it is one of the levers above.

Raised by a further 2,708 bytes (528,249 → 530,957) for M8's backlinks panel: web/src/shell/backlinks.ts, backlinks.svelte.ts, Backlinks.svelte and their CSS. About half of it is the hand-written response validation, which AGENTS.md §4.3 requires — every field there reaches the DOM and a `path` that is not a string reaches an attribute — so it is not the part to cut. The panel reuses the note tree's row, heading and empty-state classes rather than restating them, which is why the CSS share is small. §9.5 is a required M8 deliverable, the growth is measured rather than estimated, and it changes none of the reasoning above: the 355 KB of WASM is still where the budget is lost and still where the fix is.

Raised by a further 2,685 bytes (530,957 → 533,642) for M8's transclusion (§9.2): web/src/editor/embed.ts, embed-view.ts and links.ts, web/src/shell/open-note.ts, and the CSS for the embed container and the content inside it. The two response validators are again about a third of it and are again the part AGENTS.md §4.3 requires — the `html` field reaches the page as markup and the `note` field reaches a tab id. The rest is the node view, which is what makes `![[Note]]` render as anything at all: through M7 it rendered as the literal text `[[Note]]`. Nothing here is on the critical path by choice — an embed resolves at render time (§9.2), so the code has to be in the bundle that renders a note. Measured rather than estimated, and it changes none of the reasoning above: the 356 KB of WASM is still where the budget is lost and still where the fix is.

Raised by a further 2,055 bytes (533,642 → 535,697) for M8's tag pane (§9.3): web/src/shell/tags.ts, tags.svelte.ts, TagPane.svelte and their CSS. The two response validators are again about a third of it and are again what AGENTS.md §4.3 requires — a `key` from this response is interpolated into a request URL and a count reaches a row's label. The pane reuses the note tree's row, heading and empty-state classes, so the CSS share is nine lines. It is on the critical path because it renders inside the workspace shell, which is what a note page mounts; a sidebar panel that loaded separately would trade 2 KB of bundle for a round trip on first open. Measured rather than estimated, and it changes none of the reasoning above: the 356 KB of WASM is still where the budget is lost and still where the fix is.

Raised by a further 2,338 bytes (535,697 → 538,035) for M8's outline pane (§9.5): web/src/editor/outline.ts, web/src/shell/outline.ts, outline.svelte.ts, Outline.svelte and their CSS. There is no response validator in this one — the outline is read from the open document rather than fetched — so the bytes are the section arithmetic (which blocks a heading owns, where a reorder puts them) and the pane. It is on the critical path because the section move is a ProseMirror transaction and the editor is what holds one; a §9.5 outline that could not reorder would be a list of links. Measured rather than estimated, and it changes none of the reasoning above: the 356 KB of WASM is still where the budget is lost and still where the fix is.

Raised by a further 2,881 bytes (538,035 → 540,916) for M8's rename (§6.6): web/src/shell/rename.ts, RenamePrompt.svelte, the two commands and the confirm flow in CommandCenter.svelte, and the dialog's CSS. About a third is the response validator and the refusal wording — AGENTS.md §4.3 requires the first, and §6.5 requires the second to stay vague, which is prose that cannot be shortened without saying more than the server did. The prompt is its own component rather than a third mode of Palette.svelte because it is a form and not a list; folding it in would have cost more branches than bytes. It is on the critical path because the commands are registered by the workspace shell, which is what a note page mounts. Measured rather than estimated, and it changes none of the reasoning above: the 356 KB of WASM is still where the budget is lost and still where the fix is.

Raised by a further 3,375 bytes (540,916 → 544,291) for M8's local graph (§9.4): web/src/shell/graph.ts, graph-layout.ts, graph.svelte.ts, LocalGraph.svelte and their CSS. The largest single share is again the response validator, which AGENTS.md §4.3 requires and which is doing more work here than in the panels before it — a node's `key` reaches a DOM id, its `hop` reaches the arithmetic that positions it, and an edge naming a node that is not in the list has to be dropped rather than drawn as a line to nowhere. The layout is the next share and it is the reason the panel needs no Web Worker, no animation frame and no physics library: concentric rings are about eighty lines of trigonometry, where a force simulation would have been a dependency on the critical path. It is on the critical path because it renders inside the workspace shell, which is what a note page mounts. Measured rather than estimated, and it changes none of the reasoning above: the 356 KB of WASM is still where the budget is lost and still where the fix is.

keystroke-to-paint.reason: A measurement limit rather than a regression, and recorded rather than waved away. The figure is a double-requestAnimationFrame from the keydown, so it includes the wait for the next vsync boundary: 16.4 ms is one 60 Hz frame, which is the answer 'the keystroke made the next frame' rounded up to the frame it made. The technique cannot resolve better than that, and Event Timing — which could — is quantised to 8 ms by Chromium and so cannot either. What it does still catch is the failure the budget exists for: a keystroke costing two or three frames. Removing this entry needs a sub-frame technique, not a faster keystroke. SPEC §21.4.

longest-task.reason: A real finding, on the throttled mobile profile only: the longest main-thread task during a cold start is 65 ms against a 50 ms budget, and it is in bootstrap — instantiating a 945 KB WASM module and mounting the editor. Same root cause as the bundle breach above, so the same fix order applies and this number should be re-measured after it. Desktop is inside budget and is deliberately not recorded here, so a desktop regression still fails the build.
